# unpatched

> unpatched tells you when software you run (a firewall, a NAS, self-hosted apps, databases) is affected by a vulnerability: which version to upgrade to, and whether it is being exploited. It checks a list of what you run (`unpatched.yml`) against open data every day, in a GitHub Action, and opens an issue only when something needs action. It needs no account or API key.

It is not a scanner for code dependencies or container images; use OSV-Scanner or Trivy for that.

## Guide

- [What is unpatched](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/index.html): What unpatched does, who it is for, and what it is not.
- [Start with GitHub](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/start-github.html): Set up unpatched in a private GitHub repository in five minutes: two files, a first manual run, optional chat channels.
- [Start with the command line](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/start-cli.html): Install the unpatched command, write unpatched.yml, run a check, and use the exit codes in scripts and cron.
- [Start with Docker](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/start-docker.html): Run unpatched from the ghcr.io image on a homelab server or NAS, on a schedule, with state kept in a mounted folder.
- [Config reference](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/config.html): Every key of unpatched.yml with type, default and meaning, and examples for the stack, ignore entries, thresholds and notifications.
- [Findings and rules](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/findings.html): What a finding is, the four verdicts, the five buckets, how to read a GitHub issue and the JSON report, and every rule id.
- [Notifications](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/notifications.html): Each way unpatched tells you (GitHub issues, Telegram, Slack, Discord, ntfy, webhook), its environment variable, an example message, and how state avoids repeats.
- [Catalog](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/catalog.html): The products unpatched knows (generated list with id, vendor, kind, version scheme and end of life tracking), how entries are checked, and how to ask for a new one.
- [GitHub Action](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/action.html): The amet13/unpatched Action: what it does, its inputs and outputs, permissions, and examples for pinning a version, dry runs and chat secrets.
- [Command reference](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/cli.html): Every unpatched command and option, from the program's own help, with the exit codes.
- [With an agent](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/with-an-agent.html): Use unpatched from an AI agent: the read-only MCP server and its tools, the four skills, the Claude Code plugin and Gemini CLI extension, the MCP Registry entry, and llms.txt.
- [Data](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/data.html): Every data source unpatched reads, how often the database is built, what happens when a source fails, how to verify the download, and the licenses.
- [How accurate is it](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/accuracy.html): How unpatched's verdicts are tested (the corpus, the catalog checks), and its honest limits. No measured accuracy numbers have been published yet.
- [Privacy](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/privacy.html): What leaves your machine when you run unpatched: the database download from GitHub and OSV queries for package items. There is no telemetry.
- [FAQ](https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/guide/faq.html): Answers to common questions: why not Dependabot, Trivy or OpenCVE, why a finding is unknown, why a product is unverified, public repositories, and schedule pauses.
